translations.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: 「It should read 「Liu Lingyi」; Deng Wan's biography can verify this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation notes: 「The name should read 「Liu Lingyi」, as Deng Wan's biography confirms.

sentences.zh: 下四年亦作『劉靈遺』。

translations.literal: In the fourth year below it also reads 「Liu Lingyi」.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year below also has 「Liu Lingyi」.

sentences.zh: 」按張說是，今改正。

translations.literal: 」According to Zhang, this is correct; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhang is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 以游擊將軍垣閎為益州刺史 「垣閎」各本並作「垣閬」。

translations.literal: Colonel of Fast Cavalry Yuan Hong was made Inspector of Yizhou: In all editions 「Yuan Hong」 appears as 「Yuan Lang」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Yuan Hong was made Inspector of Yizhou」: all editions read 「Yuan Lang」 for 「Yuan Hong」.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記云：「垣閬，大明三年已為竟陵王誕所殺，見垣護之傳。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: 「Yuan Lang had already been killed by Prince Xiuofan of Jingling in the third year of Daming, as seen in the biography of Yuan Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation notes: 「Yuan Lang had already been killed by Prince Xiuofan of Jingling in Daming year 3, per the biography of Yuan Huzhi.

sentences.zh: 此為垣閎之誤。

translations.literal: This is an error for Yuan Hong.
translations.idiomatic: This is an error for Yuan Hong.

sentences.zh: 」按張說是，今改正。

translations.literal: 」According to Zhang, this is correct; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhang is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞羊希為廣州刺史 「羊希」各本並作「羊南」，據羊玄保傳，兄子希時由御史中丞出為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Censorate Yang Xi was made Inspector of Guangzhou: In all editions 「Yang Xi」 appears as 「Yang Nan」; according to the biography of Yang Xuanbao, his nephew's son Xi was then transferred from Supervisor of the Censorate to Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 「Yang Xi was made Inspector of Guangzhou」: all editions read 「Yang Nan」 for 「Yang Xi」; Yang Xuanbao's biography shows his nephew's son Xi leaving the censorate for Guangzhou at this time.

sentences.zh: 「南」字誤，今改正。

translations.literal: The character 「Nan」 is wrong; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 「Nan」 is erroneous; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 珍奇子超越為北冀州刺史 孫虨宋書考論云：「劉勔傳，超越為北豫州刺史，非北冀州。」

translations.literal: Zhen Qizi's son Chaoyue was made Inspector of Northern Jizhou: Sun Bin's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「In Liu Yan's biography, Chaoyue was Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, not Northern Jizhou.」
translations.idiomatic: 「Chaoyue was made Inspector of Northern Jizhou」: Sun Bin's Critical Study notes that Liu Yan's biography makes him Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, not Northern Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 右光祿大夫車騎將軍護軍將軍王玄謨薨 三朝本、北監本、毛本、殿本作「右光祿大夫」，局本及王玄謨傳作「左光祿大夫」。

translations.literal: Right Grand Master of the Palace, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and General Who Protects the Army Wang Xuamo died: The Three-Dynasties edition, Beijian edition, Mao edition, and Palace edition read 「Right Grand Master of the Palace」; the Bureau edition and Wang Xuamo's biography read 「Left Grand Master of the Palace」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Wang Xuamo died as Right Grand Master of the Palace, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and General Who Protects the Army」: the Three-Dynasties, Beijian, Mao, and Palace editions read 「Right Grand Master of the Palace」; the Bureau edition and his biography read 「Left Grand Master of the Palace」.

sentences.zh: 三月己未 下有戊辰。

translations.literal: Third month, jiwei day—below this there is wuchen.
translations.idiomatic: 「Third month, jiwei day」: the text below also has wuchen.

sentences.zh: 按是月丙子朔，無己未、戊辰。

translations.literal: According to this, that month's bingzi was the first day; there was no jiwei or wuchen.
translations.idiomatic: That month's bingzi was the first day; neither jiwei nor wuchen occurred.

sentences.zh: 二十日乙未，二十三日戊戌。

translations.literal: The twentieth day was yiwei, and the twenty-third day was wuxu.
translations.idiomatic: The twentieth day was yiwei and the twenty-third wuxu.

sentences.zh: 己未或乙未之譌，戊辰或戊戌之譌。

translations.literal: Jiwei is probably a corruption of yiwei, and wuchen is probably a corruption of wuxu.
translations.idiomatic: 「Jiwei」 is likely a corruption of 「yiwei」, and 「wuchen」 of 「wuxu」.

sentences.zh: 以軍司馬劉靈遺為梁南秦二州刺史 孫虨宋書考論云：「軍上脫一字。」

translations.literal: Army Chief Clerk Liu Lingyi was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces: Sun Bin's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「One character is missing above 「Army」.」
translations.idiomatic: 「Liu Lingyi was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin」: Sun Bin's Critical Study notes one missing character before 「Army」.

sentences.zh: 南譙太守孫奉伯為交州刺史 「南譙」各本並作「譙南」，據州郡志訂正。

translations.literal: Sun Fengbo, Administrator of Nanqiao, was made Inspector of Jiaozhou: In all editions 「Nanqiao」 appears as 「Qiaonan」; it is corrected according to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: 「Sun Fengbo was made Inspector of Jiaozhou」: all editions read 「Qiaonan」 for 「Nanqiao」; corrected per the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies.

sentences.zh: 殺刺史羊希 「羊希」各本並譌「羊南」，據南史、建康實錄、通鑑及本書羊玄保傳兄子希附傳改正。

translations.literal: Inspector Yang Xi was killed: In all editions 「Yang Xi」 is corrupted as 「Yang Nan」; it is corrected according to the Southern History, the Veritable Records of Jiankang, the Comprehensive Mirror, and the appended biography of nephew's son Xi in the biography of Yang Xuanbao in this book.
translations.idiomatic: 「Inspector Yang Xi was killed」: all editions corrupt 「Yang Xi」 as 「Yang Nan」; corrected per the Southern History, Veritable Records of Jiankang, Comprehensive Mirror, and Yang Xuanbao's biography in this book.

sentences.zh: 復減郡縣田祿之半 「田祿」各本及通鑑並作「田租」。

translations.literal: The field stipends of commanderies and counties were again reduced by half: In all editions and the Comprehensive Mirror this reads 「field rent」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Field stipends … again reduced by half」: all editions and the Comprehensive Mirror read 「field rent」.

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，決非專制帝王之所肯為，當是減削郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: According to this, a general halving of land rent throughout the realm is not something an autocratic emperor would willingly do; this must mean reducing the field stipends of officials in commanderies and counties by half.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of land rent empire-wide is not something an autocratic ruler would do; this must mean halving officials' field stipends in commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「田祿」，是。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Jiankang reads 「field stipends」; this is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Jiankang reads 「field stipends」, which is correct.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: It is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 丙申東海王褘改封廬江王 各本並脫去「丙申」二字，據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Prince Hui of Donghai was changed in enfeoffment to Prince of Lujiang: All editions alike omit the two characters 「bingshen」; they are supplied according to the Southern History and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: 「On bingshen, Prince Hui of Donghai was changed to Prince of Lujiang」: all editions omit 「bingshen」; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳 各本並作「乙未」，按是月乙巳朔，無乙未。

translations.literal: Fifth month, yisi day: In all editions this appears as 「yiwei」; according to this, that month's yisi was the first day, and there was no yiwei.
translations.idiomatic: 「Fifth month, yisi day」: all editions read 「yiwei」; that month's yisi was the first day, so 「yiwei」 is impossible.

sentences.zh: 下有十九日癸亥。

translations.literal: Below this there is the nineteenth day guihai.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteenth day below is guihai.

sentences.zh: 此乙未當是乙巳之誤，今改正。

translations.literal: This yiwei must be an error for yisi; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 「Yiwei」 is an error for 「yisi」; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 以南康相劉勃為交州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「劉勔傳，有弟斅，泰始中，為寧朔將軍、交州刺史，於道遇病卒。

translations.literal: Liu Bo, Chancellor of Nankang, was made Inspector of Jiaozhou: Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: 「In Liu Yan's biography there is a younger brother Jiao who, in the Taishi era, was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jiaozhou and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: 「Liu Bo was made Inspector of Jiaozhou」: Zhang Senkai's collation notes: 「Liu Yan's biography mentions a younger brother Jiao who in the Taishi era was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jiaozhou and died en route.

sentences.zh: 勃、斅形近，當即一人。」

translations.literal: Bo and Jiao are graphically similar; they must be the same person.」
translations.idiomatic: 「Bo」 and 「Jiao」 are graphically similar and must denote the same person.」

sentences.zh: 以輔國將軍沈文靖為東青州刺史 「沈文靖」沈文秀傳及通鑑作「沈文靜」。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Shen Wenjing was made Inspector of Eastern Qingzhou: In Shen Wenxiu's biography and the Comprehensive Mirror the name is written with a different final character.
translations.idiomatic: 「Shen Wenjing was made Inspector of Eastern Qingzhou」: Shen Wenxiu's biography and the Comprehensive Mirror write the name with a different final character.

sentences.zh: 尋劫制科罪 「劫」各本並作「剏」。

translations.literal: Soon afterward plundering was punished by statute: In all editions 「plunder」 appears as 「create」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Soon afterward plundering was punished by statute」: all editions read 「create」 for 「plunder」.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「當云劫制，剏字誤。

translations.literal: Sun Bin's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「It should read plundering by statute; the character 「create」 is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bin's Critical Study: 「The text should read plundering by statute; 「create」 is wrong.

sentences.zh: 」按孫說是，今改正。

translations.literal: 」According to Sun, this is correct; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 」Sun is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 立晉平王休祐子宣曜為南平王 各本並脫「立」字，據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Xuanyao, son of Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, was established as Prince of Nanping: All editions alike omit the character 「establish」; it is supplied according to the Southern History and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: 「Xuanyao was established as Prince of Nanping」: all editions omit 「establish」; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 息事衡樊 「息」各本並作「自」，據元龜二一三及六四五改正。

translations.literal: Rest the affairs of Heng and Fan: In all editions 「rest」 appears as 「self」; it is corrected according to Yuan Gui 213 and 645.
translations.idiomatic: 「Rest the affairs of Heng and Fan」: all editions read 「self」 for 「rest」; corrected per Yuan Gui 213 and 645.

sentences.zh: 輔師將軍孟次陽為兗州刺史 各本並脫「次」字，據阮佃夫傳、殷琰傳補。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the Army Meng Ciyang was made Inspector of Yanzhou: All editions alike omit the character 「ci」; it is supplied according to the biographies of Ruan Tainfu and Yin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: 「Meng Ciyang was made Inspector of Yanzhou」: all editions omit 「ci」; restored from the biographies of Ruan Tainfu and Yin Yan.

sentences.zh: 以征北大將軍南徐州刺史桂陽王休範為中書監中軍將軍揚州刺史 「中軍將軍」各本並作「中將軍」，據桂陽王休範傳補。

translations.literal: Grand General Who Campaigns North, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General of the Central Army, and Inspector of Yangzhou: In all editions 「General of the Central Army」 appears as 「Central General」; it is supplied according to the biography of Prince Xiufan of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: 「Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General of the Central Army, and Inspector of Yangzhou」: all editions read 「Central General」 for 「General of the Central Army」; restored from his biography.

sentences.zh: 輔師將軍建安王世子伯融為廣州刺史 各本並脫「伯」字。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the Army, heir of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, Bo Rong, was made Inspector of Guangzhou: All editions alike omit the character 「Bo」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Bo Rong, heir of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, was made Inspector of Guangzhou」: all editions omit 「Bo」.

sentences.zh: 據始安王休仁傳補。

translations.literal: It is supplied according to the biography of Prince Xiuren of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: Restored from the biography of Prince Xiuren of Shian.

sentences.zh: 新除吏部尚書褚淵為尚書右僕射 「右僕射」各本及通鑑並作「左僕射」。

translations.literal: Newly appointed Minister of Personnel Chu Yuan was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: In all editions and the Comprehensive Mirror this reads 「Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Chu Yuan was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」: all editions and the Comprehensive Mirror read 「Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」.

sentences.zh: 今據南齊書褚淵傳、南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: It is now emended according to the biography of Chu Yuan in the Book of Qi, the Southern History, and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per Chu Yuan's biography in the Book of Qi, the Southern History, and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊午 「十一月」各本並作「十月」。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, wuwu day: In all editions 「eleventh month」 appears as 「tenth month」; it is emended according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: 「Winter, eleventh month, wuwu day」: all editions read 「tenth month」 for 「eleventh month」; emended per the Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 據建康實錄改。

translations.literal: It is emended according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per the Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 按十月丙戌朔，無戊午。

translations.literal: According to this, the tenth month's bingxu was the first day; there was no wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month's bingxu was the first day; wuwu did not occur.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯朔，初四日戊午。

translations.literal: The eleventh month's yimao was the first day; the fourth day was wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month's yimao was the first day; the fourth day was wuwu.

sentences.zh: 以右衞將軍張興世為雍州刺史 各本並脫「世」字。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi, General of the Right Guard, was made Inspector of Yongzhou: In all editions the character 「shi」 has been dropped.
translations.idiomatic: 「Zhang Xingshi was made Inspector of Yongzhou」: all editions omit 「shi」.

sentences.zh: 據張興世傳補。

translations.literal: It is supplied according to Zhang Xingshi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Restored per Zhang Xingshi's biography.

sentences.zh: 於華林園含芳堂講周易 各本並脫「含」字，據元龜一九二補。

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes was lectured upon in Hanfang Hall in Hualin Garden: In all editions the character 「han」 has been dropped; it is supplied according to Yuan Gui 192.
translations.idiomatic: 「Lectures on the Classic of Changes in Hanfang Hall, Hualin Garden」: all editions omit 「han」; restored from Yuan Gui 192.

sentences.zh: 改騧為馬邊瓜 三朝本、北監本、毛本、殿本無「馬」字，今據局本及魏書島夷傳、南史補。

translations.literal: 「Gua」 was changed to horse beside melon: The Three-Dynasties, Beijian, Mao, and Palace editions lack the character 「horse」; it is now supplied according to the Bureau edition and the biography of the island barbarians in the Book of Wei and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 「Changing gua to horse-beside-melon」: the Three-Dynasties, Beijian, Mao, and Palace editions lack 「horse」; supplied per the Bureau edition, the Book of Wei, and the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 職局以之坐者數十人 魏書島夷傳、南史、建康實錄「坐」下有「死」字。

translations.literal: Several tens in the office staff were punished on that account: In the biography of the island barbarians in the Book of Wei, the Southern History, and the Veritable Records of Jiankang, the character 「die」 appears below 「punished」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Several tens in the office staff were punished」: the Book of Wei, Southern History, and Veritable Records of Jiankang add 「die」 after 「punished」.

sentences.zh: 並日料祿俸 各本並同。

translations.literal: All alike received daily allotments of stipend salary: All editions are the same.
translations.idiomatic: 「Daily allotments of stipend salary」: all editions agree.

sentences.zh: 魏書島夷傳作「普斷祿奉」。

translations.literal: The biography of the island barbarians in the Book of Wei reads 「stipends and salaries were cut off universally」.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei reads 「stipends and salaries were cut off universally」.

sentences.zh: 南史及通鑑作「並斷祿奉」。

translations.literal: The Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror read 「stipends and salaries were cut off alike」.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror read 「stipends and salaries were cut off alike」.

sentences.zh: 列見眾篇 三朝本作「列」。

translations.literal: Set forth separately in the various chapters: The Three-Dynasties edition reads 「set forth」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Set forth separately in the various chapters」: the Three-Dynasties edition reads 「set forth」.

sentences.zh: 北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「別」。

translations.literal: The Beijian, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 「separately」.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijian, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 「separately」.

sentences.zh: 張元濟校勘記云：「所見處不止一篇，故云列見眾篇。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanji's collation notes say: 「The places seen are not limited to one chapter; hence it says they are set forth separately in the various chapters.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji's collation notes: 「The deeds appear in more than one chapter, hence the phrase about the various chapters.」

sentences.zh: 本無卓爾之資 「資」各本作「姿」，據南史改。

translations.literal: He fundamentally lacked outstanding talent: In all editions 「talent」 appears as 「bearing」; it is emended according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: 「Fundamentally lacked outstanding talent」: all editions read 「bearing」 for 「talent」; emended per the Southern History.
